PullRequest.Title: Make action widget menu items directly clickable by Playwright
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes #334755.

## Summary
Make ordinary and tabbed action-widget menu items directly clickable by Playwright, without forced clicks or a preliminary hover.

- Remove the temporary pointer shield; retain the outside-click backdrop.
- Preserve keyboard focus beneath a stationary cursor by ignoring initial mouse-over and zero-delta movement until pointer interaction enables hover.
- Update automation helpers to use normal clicks and fixtures to simulate deliberate movement.

Native CSS hover styling remains intentional and does not change the keyboard target. Preserves the focus intent of #157694 / #157718.

## Validation
- 39 CI checks passed; only the human approval gate is pending. Fresh Copilot review on `2cf00ac0bc4`: no findings.
- 69 targeted unit tests, 2 smoke tests, and 6 stable model-picker fixture variants; no baseline changes.
- Live Code OSS: ordinary and redesigned picker clicks, stationary-pointer keyboard focus, configuration, and search-result clicks passed.
- Chromium-emulated touch/pen: opening, first-tap selection, pen hover, and outside dismissal passed in the live workbench; provider-tab touch switching passed in a fixture.
- Real native integrated browser: automated menu/modal hide-and-restore checks passed. User manually confirmed picker/card overlap, no click-through, and working page input after dismissal.

Physical touch/pen hardware was not tested; macOS permissions prevented automated OS-composited capture/input.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The permanent subscription, one-way state transition, and ListView's per-event mapper/ancestor walk are directly established in repository code, and the affected widgets are product-facing code-action and chat picker menus. Exact CPU cost varies with pointer polling rate and popup dwell time, which limits severity but not mechanism confidence.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Main-thread DOM ancestor traversal and one IListMouseEvent allocation for each mousemove
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The cost repeats at pointer-event frequency for the entire lifetime of every open action list (including code-action and chat model-picker menus), rather than only for the first non-zero movement; high-polling mice can generate hundreds to thousands of events per second.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased main-thread CPU and allocation/GC pressure while moving the pointer over an open action menu, with avoidable input/rendering contention on high-event-rate devices.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The pointer shield handled POINTER_MOVE only until the first movement, then removed itself from the DOM, so later pointer motion did not execute this activation work.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The diff registers List.onMouseMove for the full widget lifetime. Although the callback body becomes a no-op once _ignoreInitialHover is false, ListView still maps every DOM mousemove through toMouseEvent before invoking it.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 961 registers `this._list.onMouseMove(...)` in the widget-wide disposable store; lines 962-965 show that only the first non-zero event has useful behavior, while all subsequent mapped events remain subscribed. The deleted pointer-block implementation removed its event-receiving DOM node on the first POINTER_MOVE.
Findings.Title: Dispose the one-shot mousemove listener after activation
Findings.Impact: After the first movement over an open code-action, dropdown, or model-picker list, all later movements still perform DOM target-to-row resolution and allocate a mapped list event. This scales with mouse polling rate and can add avoidable CPU/GC pressure while the popup is being interacted with.
Findings.Evidence: ListView.onMouseMove is an Event.map over a DOM `mousemove` emitter (`src/vs/base/browser/ui/list/listView.ts:1159`), and the mapper calls `toMouseEvent`, which invokes `getItemIndexFromEventTarget`; that method walks ancestors, calls `scrollableElement.contains`, reads `data-index`, and allocates the returned IListMouseEvent (`listView.ts:1165-1169,1541-1559`). The new callback only needs the first non-zero movement, because it permanently sets `_ignoreInitialHover = false`, but the subscription at the changed line remains registered until the entire ActionListWidget is disposed.
Findings.Recommendation: Use a raw disposable `mousemove` listener on the list element and dispose/clear that listener immediately after the first non-zero movement (while retaining mousedown activation), so row hover continues via the existing `onMouseOver` handler without permanent per-move mapping.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open an ordinary action widget (for example code actions or a chat/dropdown picker) and move the pointer across its rows.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Popup construction synchronously creates the List and its DOM listeners. Each mousemove over the list is synchronously mapped by ListView.toMouseEvent/getItemIndexFromEventTarget before the new callback runs; the first non-zero movement enables hover, while later movements are unnecessary work on the input/rendering critical path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Pointer-event frequency multiplied by the duration the action list remains open; one active list normally handles the events, with a separately created submenu list doing the same when interacted with.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Browser mousemove events are processed serially on the renderer main thread; there is no batching, throttling, or listener teardown after activation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache applies. The row index is recomputed from the event target for every movement, even after `_ignoreInitialHover` is permanently false.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed permanent subscription, one-way guard, Event.map allocation, and DOM ancestor walk are directly visible in the call path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Popup dwell time and mouse polling rate vary, so the absolute CPU/GC cost is uncertain and severity is low; high-polling mice make hundreds to thousands of events per second realistic.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable low-severity repeated work: the diff replaces a first-movement-only shield path with a widget-lifetime mousemove subscription whose mapping cost continues after activation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open and interact with the tabbed chat model picker, including switching provider tabs and directly clicking a model row.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: TabbedActionListWidget constructs one active ActionList synchronously; pointer activation follows the same ListView mousemove path before row hover/click handling. Tab changes rebuild the popup/list, so each active list gets the lifetime subscription. Selection itself remains the existing delegate path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Mousemove count while the active tab's list is open; tab switches replace rather than accumulate listeners.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One popup/list is active at a time; tab replacement disposes the prior popup. UI events are serialized on the renderer main thread with no concurrent network work introduced by these hunks.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The model collection and destination calculation are existing in-memory work. No new cache, cache miss, network fetch, IPC, filesystem call, or subprocess is introduced by the pointer changes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the repeated mousemove mapping; high that no expensive external boundary was added on this scenario.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Model counts and interaction duration vary, but event cardinality is controlled by pointer frequency rather than model count because ListView resolves only the target's ancestor chain.
Scenarios.Verdict: The same reported one-shot-listener regression applies. Removal of the full-screen pointer-block DOM node and its two listeners otherwise reduces work and does not add a separate regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or close an action/context widget over an integrated browser WebContentsView, causing overlay detection and browser visibility changes.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: DOM mutations are coalesced by MicrotaskEmitter, then BrowserOverlayManager synchronously enumerates tracked overlays, reads cached/current geometry, and hit-tests. If obscured state changes, WebContentsViewRendererFeature captures a placeholder screenshot and invokes visibility changes before the browser can be hidden or shown.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most the existing transition-triggered capture for an obscuring overlay, plus the pre-existing screenshot cadence; not per pointer event and unchanged by this diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The tracked context view already caused the same obscured-state transition and screenshot path; the removed pointer block was only a hit-test exclusion inside that context view.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The screenshot supplies the placeholder before/while the native browser view is hidden; it is downstream of an actual obscured-state transition.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Set native browser view visibility through `browserViewService.setVisible`.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One hide when obscured state transitions true and one show when it transitions false, state-guarded; unchanged by the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Opening/closing the tracked context view produced the same visibility transitions before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Hiding occurs after a one-frame defer; showing is initiated immediately when the overlay clears.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of tracked overlays and overlay state transitions, not action-list row count or pointer frequency.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Mutation notifications are microtask-coalesced. Visibility changes are state-guarded, and hide is deferred by one animation frame; screenshot/service promises can be in flight, but the diff adds no fan-out or new concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Overlay rectangles are cached while observers are connected and invalidated by element/style mutation observers. Removing `context-view-pointerBlock` from exclusions matches removal of that DOM element; it does not invalidate a useful cache or create new misses.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the overlay-manager-to-renderer call path and downstream service calls are explicit, and the removed class is no longer emitted by the changed action widgets.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of simultaneous overlays is typically small; exact screenshot/IPC latency is platform-dependent, but neither boundary's count or placement is increased by the diff.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding. The diff removes a DOM layer/mutations and a now-unused exclusion; it does not introduce or amplify layout, hit-test, screenshot, or IPC work.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 12 changed files and all diff pages. One low-severity repeated-work finding was submitted for the permanent mousemove mapping added to every ActionListWidget. Pointer-block removal, tabbed-picker behavior, overlay hit-testing, browser-view screenshot/visibility boundaries, tests, automation helpers, and documentation introduced no other performance regression. The PR does not establish a shipped performance-regression fix suitable for blame-based learning.
